rounds.text: Competent Automobiles Company Ltd is trading at a heavily discounted valuation, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.57x against a book value of ₹ 629 and a sector benchmark of 1.91x [E2, E7], alongside a modest P/E of 9.12x [E1]. This disconnect from intrinsic value is further underscored by a discounted cash flow model placing value at ₹ 821 per share, offering a substantial 56.4% margin of safety [E37, E38]. Operational momentum is strong, demonstrated by a 25% compounded sales growth and 30% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15], backed by stellar cash generation where operating cash flow reached ₹ 80 Cr and covered 97% of operating profit [E27, E29]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF implies that the current price of ₹ 358 already prices in a negative 1.6% earnings growth, ignoring the reality of accelerating fundamentals and a recent 41% year-on-year surge in net profit [E2, E39, E53]. Conceded: debt exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.09x and borrowings at ₹ 422 Cr [E30, E32].

Competent Automobiles Company Ltd is severely under-appreciated by the market, trading at an exceptionally low price-to-earnings ratio of 9.12x and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.57x against a book value of ₹ 629 [E1, E2]. This heavy discount is completely detached from the underlying financial momentum, highlighted by a robust 25% compounded sales growth and a 30% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15], alongside expectations for a good quarter [E44]. Crucially, this profit generation is backed by elite cash conversion of 3.81x, yielding ₹ 80 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 59 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E26, E27, E28]. A discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic worth at ₹ 821 per share, leaving an expansive margin of safety of 56.4% [E37, E38]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that the current market price of ₹ 358 priced in a negative 1.6% earnings growth, completely ignoring the reality of accelerating results and rising institutional interest from domestic buyers [E37, E39, E41]. conceded: [E30], [E32]

While the bull leans on cheap valuation multiples like a 9.12x P/E and a 0.57x P/B [E1, E2], these metrics mask persistent structural weaknesses, notably a chronically low return on equity of 6% to 6.69% and a 3-year median ROE of just 7% [E13, E20, E46], alongside an inconsistent operating-margin trend over the last three years [E24]. The cited growth figures and cash generation [E14, E15, E27] are overshadowed by heavy financial leverage where total borrowings expanded to ₹ 422 Cr in March 2026, driving the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.09x—meaning debt outright exceeds net worth—and resulting in a flagged low interest coverage ratio [E30, E32, E45]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on intrinsic value models [E37, E38] ignores that the company’s actual share price performance has cratered by -11% over the past year and achieved a meager 3% compounded return over three years [E18, E19]. conceded: [E14], [E15], [E27]
